questions.q: What does SQL Server's Change Tracking feature actually record for a changed row?
options: That the row (identified by primary key) changed, tagged with a version number — not the actual old/new values
The full before and after values of every column in the row
A screenshot of the row before and after the change
Nothing — Change Tracking only tracks schema changes, not data
questions.explain: Change Tracking is deliberately lightweight — it tracks which rows changed by key and version, and the consumer re-queries the base table for current values.

questions.q: How does Change Data Capture (CDC) obtain its change information?
options: By reading the transaction log via a SQL Server Agent job and writing before/after row images to change tables
By polling the table with a scheduled SELECT every second
By reading the query plan cache
It requires no background process at all
questions.explain: CDC's capture job reads the transaction log and populates dedicated change tables with full row images.

questions.q: What is the key functional difference between Change Tracking and CDC?
options: Change Tracking tells you which rows changed; CDC additionally captures the actual old and new column values
Change Tracking is Enterprise-only; CDC is available in every edition
CDC cannot track deletes, only inserts and updates
Change Tracking requires SQL Server Agent; CDC does not
questions.explain: Change Tracking answers 'which rows changed'; CDC answers 'what exactly changed, to what values,' at a higher storage and I/O cost.

questions.q: What is a real cost/dependency of using Change Data Capture, per this lesson?
options: It requires SQL Server Agent to be running, since the capture job depends on it, and adds more storage and I/O than Change Tracking
It requires disabling the transaction log entirely
It only works with in-memory OLTP tables
It cannot be used alongside regular transactions
questions.explain: CDC's capture job runs as an Agent job and reading/storing full row images costs meaningfully more than Change Tracking's key-based approach.

questions.q: A downstream process only needs to know which rows to re-fetch from a table to refresh a cache. Which feature fits, per this lesson's guidance?
options: Change Tracking — it's simpler, cheaper, and sufficient when only 'which rows changed' matters
CDC, because it is always the safer default choice
Neither feature can support this use case
Only a full table scan comparison can answer this
questions.explain: When a consumer just needs to know what to re-fetch, Change Tracking is the right, lower-overhead fit; reaching for CDC here is unnecessary overhead.
